subject: science

sections.scope_note: Arizona standards deferred. This crosswalk covers Florida NGSSS Science (2016), Grade 7, and IB MYP sciences only. Rows are suggested (Label C). Science is grade-based in the adopted package, not a middle-school course code. Six clusters cover the grade list on purpose.

ib_framework_elements: MYP sciences: criterion B Inquiring and designing
MYP sciences: criterion C Processing and evaluating
rows.key_differences: Florida asks students to define a problem from the seventh-grade curriculum, distinguish replication from repetition, separate experiments from other investigations, identify variables, compare methods across fields, and explain empirical evidence and debate in the science community. MYP criteria B and C are titles only here. The Florida sentences are not IB descriptors.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Plan a short investigation, name the test variable and the outcome variable, and say how replication differs from repeating trials.

rows.topic_domain: Light, waves, heat, and energy transfer
ib_framework_elements: MYP sciences: criterion A Knowing and understanding
MYP global context: scientific and technical innovation
rows.key_differences: Florida specifies the sun’s radiation, reflection, refraction, and absorption, wave speed in materials, heat and change of state, energy transformations, conservation of energy, and heat flow. The public MYP pages do not state those laws.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Describe one energy change in a simple system and say whether heat moved from a warmer object to a cooler one.

ib_framework_elements: MYP sciences: criterion A Knowing and understanding
rows.key_differences: Florida asks students to connect fossils, genetic variation, natural selection, and extinction to the scientific theory of evolution. That content list is NGSSS. It is not an MYP syllabus.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Use one piece of fossil or variation evidence to explain a change in a population, without treating the Florida wording as an IB objective.

ib_framework_elements: MYP sciences: criterion A Knowing and understanding
rows.key_differences: Florida covers DNA and chromosomes, Punnett squares and pedigrees, meiosis and mitosis, biotechnology, food webs, named ecological relationships, and limiting factors. Schools may offer life-science courses. MYP does not require this list.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Trace energy from a producer to a consumer in a local example, and name one limiting factor.

rows.topic_domain: Scientific knowledge, theories, laws, and models
ib_framework_elements: MYP sciences: criterion A Knowing and understanding
MYP sciences: criterion D Reflecting on the impacts of science
rows.key_differences: Florida asks for a historical case where knowledge changed, the difference between theories and laws, and benefits and limits of models. Criterion titles are stored only. The 1-8 descriptors and any required case study are not IB text here.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Name one model the class uses and one limit of that model.

ib_framework_elements: MYP sciences: schools may offer earth sciences
MYP global context: globalization and sustainability
rows.key_differences: Florida specifies Earth’s layers, the rock cycle, dating methods, geologic change, plate tectonics, human impacts, and earthquakes and volcanoes. The sciences page allows earth-science courses. It does not require this list.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Explain one slow and one rapid change to Earth’s surface using plate tectonics, and name one human impact.
